parsed.summary: The PLAN-B77 implementation plan thoroughly addresses the root causes of the 512MB Fly.io OOM kill and missed jobs with solid empirical measurements. Replacing scipy with math.erf and a pure-Python Brent implementation eliminates ~54MB resident overhead. Streaming warrant JSON via ijson and incremental sector price sync slash peak allocations from ~206MB and ~173MB to bounded streaming buffers. Global heavy-job serialization via RLock with 60-minute timeouts and loop-detection prevents concurrent job stacking and event-loop blocking. Crash-loop prevention (max 2 catchup attempts, 2-strike step skipping, 6-hour resume window, 512MB disk swap safety net) is well-bounded. Acceptance tests and Playwright UI tests provide rigorous validation.

findings.issue: During the two passes of ijson parsing on the temporary contract file, Pass 1 consumes the stream to construct the warrant-to-underlying mapping. If the file pointer is not rewound before Pass 2, Pass 2 will read EOF.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly include `f.seek(0)` between Pass 1 and Pass 2 on the temporary file object before initializing the second ijson iterator.

findings.issue: If `chip_data/catchup.json` is partially written or truncated during a sudden SIGKILL or power cycle, standard JSON deserialization at boot could raise JSONDecodeError.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the `catchup.json` read in a try/except block that falls back to an empty tracking dictionary if corrupted, and use atomic write (write to temp file and rename) when persisting attempt counts.

parsed.coverage: Reviewed memory optimization (ijson, incremental sync, math.erf/brentq), execution safety (heavy RLock, event-loop guards, APScheduler overlap), startup catch-up & crash recovery (need_scan_catchup, crash step skipping, 6h resume TTL), frontend polling & caching (SWR, single-flight locks, LWC autoscale margins), and acceptance test coverage against provided server, ingester, calculator, prices, and disposal implementations.
parsed.limitations: Static code and plan review based on provided codebase and scratchpad measurements; runtime verification on Fly.io (memory behavior under Linux glibc malloc_trim and actual swap paging performance) depends on deployment.
